header: Date: 2025-07-16 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Reyes (Redwood SE), Janelle Park (Redwood SE), Leah Martin (Bluehaven CTO), Samir Patel (Bluehaven Lead Eng), Dana Ortiz (Product), Ravi Narayan (Infra)
summary: Redwood hosted API demo covering chat/text generation basics: streaming behaviour, key parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), idempotency and retry strategies, and a quick tour of the Console Optimize hints. Action items: provision sandbox, share security docs, run a 1-week pilot with benchmarks.
topics: Retry/backoff and idempotency for at-least-once vs at-most-once semantics
Console walkthrough: model catalog, per-route dashboards, Optimize suggestions
transcript:
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. We'll run through hosted chat basics and then Omar will show streaming, retries and Console.
00:12 Leah: Thanks, Maya. Quick note — we have about 30 minutes of demo and 10 for Q&A, right?
00:16 Maya: Yeah that's the plan. Samir, Dana, Ravi — feel free to jump in anytime.
00:24 Omar: Hi all, Omar here. I'll start with the streaming demo and show how we tune params. Note: some of the names in the transcript might be off; the audio auto-captures.
00:36 Samir: Cool. Our main constraints: sub-250ms p95 for short replies on mobile, and cost sensitivity — we want predictable unit cost.
00:44 Maya: Perfect, that's super common. We'll look at latency vs throughput knobs and how automatic batching and prefix caching help.
01:02 Omar: Alright sharing my screen — Console > Hosted API > Model Catalog. You can pick a curated model variant; we also show the perf profile.
01:18 Dana: Is there an easy way to pin a model variant per route?
01:21 Omar: Yep — route-level override. You can pin exact model version and quantization profile. That way rollouts are safe.
01:34 Maya: Quick caveat, the UI sometimes shows "Redwood-verifyied" spelled weird in the export — ignore that.
01:45 Omar: Now the streaming demo. I send a short prompt and you'll see partial tokens arrive as SSE chunks.
02:00 Leah: In our app we want partial replies for typing indicators but not intermediate hallucinations — how do we control that?
02:09 Omar: Good question. You can control chunk frequency by setting stream_chunk_tokens and also control when to render — e.g., wait until first punctuation. We also recommend server-side filters.
02:25 Samir: That stream_chunk_tokens param — is it per-request in the API?
02:29 Omar: Yes you include it as a generation param. Default is tuned for low latency, but you can increase chunking for fewer updates.
02:40 Maya: Also note that streaming behavior slightly varies by model family and sequence length distribution — the runtime picks optimized kernels accordingly.
03:05 Ravi: About retries — we have intermittent 5xx from our edge, what's the recommended pattern?
03:11 Omar: We recommend idempotency keys for user-visible operations. For pure chat generation you can do exponential backoff with jitter and detect partial stream receipts. If a stream failed mid-response, we suggest client-side reconciliation using an idempotency token to avoid double outputs.
03:38 Dana: Could you give an example header or field for idempotency?
03:42 Omar: Sure, add X-Idempotency-Key: <uuid> on the request. If a retry is safe, the server dedupes. For streaming we support resume tokens too in some variants but that's more advanced.
04:02 Samir: We do a lot of short messages — optimizing cost is key, what are the levers?
04:08 Omar: Main levers: max_tokens per reply, response length control via stop sequences, batching on the server side, and prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts. Also quantized model variants reduce token cost.
04:28 Leah: Is there a telemetry view for token-level cost?
04:31 Omar: Yep, Console -> Billing & Usage breaks down tokens by route, model and time window. The Optimize tab gives recommendations — e.g., "use q4_0 for inference on this workload" — those are heuristics from our Optimize engine.
04:52 Maya: Quick note on accuracy vs cost: Optimize may suggest lowering precision but we recommend A/B testing with eval prompts.
05:12 Dana: For our use-case, we need PII redaction — what's the best practice?
05:17 Omar: Client-side redaction before sending is safest. For hosted we also offer data retention controls and audit logs; we'll include SOC2 docs in the follow-up.
05:30 Maya: I'll add security docs to the action items.
05:36 Omar: Back to retry semantics — here's a pattern we often recommend: short retry window for transient 429/503 with exponential backoff (100ms -> 200ms -> 400ms), up to 3 retries, and then fallback to a lighter model or cached answer.
06:00 Samir: Fallback to lighter model — does Redwood handle automatic fallback?
06:05 Omar: Yes, you can configure routing policies. For example, primary: high-accuracy model, fallback: quantized lower-cost variant or a cached response. The platform will do automatic fallback when capacity is constrained.
06:22 Leah: How do we test failover?
06:25 Omar: We have a test harness script in the repo I can share. It simulates 503 and measures recovery and token cost.
06:35 Janelle: sending link in chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-failover (note: demo link)
06:46 Dana: About streaming partials — sometimes clients re-render partials leading to duplicates — how do we avoid duplicates?
06:52 Omar: Implement sequence-numbered chunks or idempotent render logic on client: only append new tokens since last offset. We also add chunk metadata sometimes; transcripts may show weird tokenization words like "K V cash" instead of KV cache.
07:15 Samir: Lol yeah saw that in a doc.
07:22 Maya: Moving on to parameters: temperature, top_p, and presence_penalty — short refresher and recommended defaults for chat.
07:32 Omar: For deterministic replies set temperature 0.0 and top_p 0.0. For creative options temperature 0.7 with top_p 0.9. Presence_penalty helps reduce repetition. For customer-facing answers we recommend temp 0.2-0.4.
07:58 Leah: Do you recommend per-route defaults in Console?
08:02 Omar: Exactly, route-level defaults and you can override for specific calls.
08:08 Dana: Any guidance on max_tokens? We don't want long-winded answers.
08:12 Omar: Set a sane max_tokens (e.g., 60-120) and a stop sequence like "\nUser:" or a delimiter. Also consider post-processing truncation heuristics.
08:30 Samir: Show us retry example in code?
08:33 Omar: Sure — here's a pseudocode snippet: try request with idempotency; on 5xx => exponential backoff; if exhausted => call fallback model endpoint. (Code snippet shown in chat).
09:00 Maya: We'll paste the snippet in the follow-up email.
09:06 Leah: We're interested in latency SLOs again — p95 < 250ms for short messages, p99 tolerable up to 600ms. Can you map which model families hit that?
09:16 Omar: We have perf profiles: small-gen 2x lower latency but lower quality, medium-gen balanced. I'll attach a perf spreadsheet after this call. In practice you can reach p95 ~180-220ms for short replies with autoscaling and warm KV cache.
09:38 Ravi: What about burst protection?
09:41 Omar: Dedicated reserved capacity or burst tokens help. Hosted has configurable burst pools; Dedicated gives isolation.
09:52 Dana: If we go pilot hosted and later need private for data residency, how hard is migration?
09:58 Maya: We've built migration workflows: same API surface, model pinning, and rollout policies. Private deployments require additional provisioning but code changes are minimal. We'll walk through that in the next call if needed.
10:21 Samir: Any limits on streaming concurrency per key?
10:24 Omar: Default rate limits exist; for pilot we can increase sandbox quotas. Route-based throttles are configurable.
10:32 Leah: Show us Console Optimize hints — where do we get cost vs perf suggestions?
10:36 Omar: Switching to Optimize tab: it lists suggestions like "Reduce max_tokens on route X" or "Enable prefix cache for session-heavy flows" and expected cost delta.
10:48 Dana: How reliable are those suggestions?
10:51 Janelle: They're heuristics derived from production traces — we recommend validating on sample traffic.
11:00 Maya: We also have a per-token cost estimator per route in the Console.
11:08 Samir: Great. Anything about observability for debugging streaming issues?
11:12 Omar: Traces include per-token timing, model kernel metrics, and error breakdowns. You can export to your tracing backend. We also surface root cause hints like "KV cache cold".
11:30 Leah: Can we get audit logs for data access?
11:34 Maya: Yes, you're able to configure audit retention windows; we'll include the specifics in the security packet.
11:42 Ravi: For encryption at rest, do you support customer-managed keys?
11:45 Omar: We do KMS integration for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports managed keys with an option for BYOK on enterprise plans.
12:02 Dana: Ok back to practical next steps for pilot — we want sample payloads, keys and a benchmark sheet.
12:08 Maya: Omar will provision sandbox keys and I'll send the pilot scope template.
12:14 Samir: We'll provide traffic profile and SLOs.
12:18 Leah: Budget check — what's typical cost for a week-long pilot?
12:22 Maya: It depends on tokens; we'll put an estimate in the pilot doc. We'll show both hosted and Dedicated comparatives.
12:32 Dana: Any security red flags we should be aware of?
12:36 Maya: Nothing immediate, but we'll include SOC2 report, data retention, RBAC, and SSO integration docs.
12:45 Janelle: sharing links in chat — security packet, pilot template, and quickstart guide.
13:02 Omar: Quick polish: when dealing with intermittency, prefer short retries and fallback early — long backoffs increase user wait time. Also consider optimistic UI patterns where you show partial content while final answer is reconciling.
13:22 Samir: That makes sense. We'll likely implement optimistic render + final confirmation.
13:30 Leah: Last question: do you have examples of stop sequences used in e-commerce chat?
13:35 Omar: Use clear delimiters like "\n### END" or structured JSON outputs with validateable schema. We also support function/tool calling to return structured responses.
13:50 Dana: Function calling — do you have RPC-like examples?
13:54 Omar: Yes, Console has examples for tool-calls — send tool schema, model returns arguments; we've got a demo in the repo.
14:10 Maya: Okay wrapping up — recap: Omar will provision sandbox and perf sheet; Maya send security & pricing; Bluehaven sends traffic profile and confirms SLO.
14:22 Leah: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
14:26 Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links.
14:30 (crosstalk)
42:00 [call ends]
